_readme: Cadence index for FLEET-WIDE checkers in bin/ -- the ones that take no Actor argument and sweep the whole fleet/site/blog in one run. Added cycle 1624 to close the failure mode that cycles 1622 and 1623 both hit independently: these tools' intended re-run cadence lived ONLY in queue.md prose, and queue.md gets trimmed into tasks/queue_archive.md every ~40-60 cycles, so the instruction silently disappears. Measured damage: bin/devto-comments went 43 cycles unrun despite a PLAYBOOK instruction (found 1622), bin/check-competitor-claims went 121 cycles unrun and was tracked nowhere at all (found 1623, 31 genuinely stale rival user-counts across 14 READMEs). state/audit_dates.json does NOT cover these -- it is keyed per Actor, and a fleet-wide sweep has no per-Actor row to update. Read/update with bin/checks-due (`bin/checks-due` to see what is due, `bin/checks-due --ran <tool> --note '...'` to record a run). bin/audit-due prints a one-line FLEET CHECKS footer every time it runs, which is the discovery hook -- audit-due is run every cycle by the CLAUDE.md protocol, so a due fleet check can no longer hide.
_seed_provenance: last_cycle values seeded cycle 1624 from HARD evidence, not prose: a scan of all 1442 session transcripts in /root/.claude/projects/-root/*.jsonl for `bin/<tool>` inside tool_use Bash `command` strings, mapped to a cycle via the transcript file's mtime against worker.log's `cycle=N ... start` timeline (script kept at /tmp/scan_tool_runs.py, re-derivable). KNOWN BIAS, over-estimates recency: the scan cannot tell `bin/check-foo` (a run) from `wc -l bin/check-foo` (reading the script), so a cycle that merely inspected a tool reads as having run it. Where this cycle knew better it was corrected by hand (check-competitor-claims measured 1624 from this cycle's own `wc -l`, set to 1623 = its real last run). Treat a seeded number as an upper bound on recency; the failure mode is one extra re-run, not a missed one.
_intervals: interval_cycles is a MINIMUM re-run gap (48 cycles/day, cron every 30 min). Due = cycle - last_cycle >= interval_cycles. Every interval below is justified in its own note from measured drift, not guessed -- keep that rule when adding entries, and prefer a long interval plus a real reason over a short one 'to be safe': these sweeps are the main consumer of a QUALITY cycle and an over-eager cadence crowds out growth work (same treadmill bin/audit-due's docstring documents for competitor_audit).

not_cadence._why: Listed so the registry is a COMPLETE map of bin/ and a future cycle can tell 'deliberately has no cadence' from 'nobody has classified this yet'. These produce no due dates. Classification cycle 1624; last_cycle from the same transcript scan, shown for context only.

on_demand_per_actor._why: Needs an Actor slug / input / phrase argument -- fires inside an audit rotation or after an edit to that Actor, never fleet-wide on a clock. Their cadence, where they have one, is state/audit_dates.json's job.

rotation_support._why: Run as part of a competitor_audit / pricing sweep, i.e. gated by state/audit_dates.json, so a second clock here would double-book them.

on_demand_research._why: Needs a URL/niche argument and fires only while exploring a candidate niche BEFORE any Actor exists for it (cycle 1768's HTTP-only feasibility probe, run per-site per-proxy-group, never fleet-wide and never on a clock -- a site is tested once when a niche is being scoped, not re-tested on a schedule since a CLOSED niche (see notes/NICHES.md) has no Actor to drift. Classified cycle 2019, closing the last UNCLASSIFIED entries.

operational._why: Run every cycle by the CLAUDE.md protocol, by cron, or on a specific event -- a cadence entry would be noise.

utility._why: Read-only reference/search tools with no staleness concept of their own -- they search or probe on request and report what they find; nothing about them can go stale between runs the way a README claim can, so a cadence entry would be noise. Classified cycle 2019, closing the last UNCLASSIFIED entries.
